findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed LoadError::Io variant

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or missing field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input causes a panic instead of returning a typed parse/validation error
findings.fix: use .map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) and return Result, removing unwrap entirely

findings.problem: parts[0] direct indexing without bounds check on split result
findings.failure_mode: empty or whitespace-only line produces zero-length parts vec, causing panic on index access
findings.fix: use parts.first().ok_or(ParseError::EmptyField) or destructure with pattern matching

findings.problem: parts[1] direct indexing without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma-delimited field (or empty line) causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingValue) to handle short lines gracefully

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs unchecked narrowing cast
findings.failure_mode: any u32 value > 65535 silently truncates to u16, producing silently incorrect domain data
findings.fix: use u32::try_into().map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOverflow) or parse directly with u16::from_str

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs I/O inside domain parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: side-effecting print leaks into what should be pure data transformation; breaks determinism and testability
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the parsing function; logging belongs in the shell layer only

findings.problem: file I/O, parsing, logging, and Vec allocation are all fused in a single function
findings.failure_mode: no separation between imperative shell (I/O) and pure functional core (parsing/calculation); violates bounded-resource and typed-error principles
findings.fix: split into shell fn load_frames(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads file, and pure fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> that handles parsing

findings.problem: No error types defined; all failures collapse into panic via unwrap()
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish between file-not-found, parse-invalid, missing-field, value-overflow, or allocation failures
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), Allocation } and enum ParseError { EmptyField, MissingValue, InvalidValue, ValueOverflow } with From<io::Error> impl

findings.problem: println!() return value (Result) is discarded with let _ = pattern implicit
findings.failure_mode: write failure to stdout is silently ignored; must-use result contract violated
findings.fix: remove the println call entirely (see functional_core_imperative_shell finding)

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no newtypes, no validation, no typestate
findings.failure_mode: any code can construct Record with empty name, out-of-range value, or invalid state; illegal states are representable
findings.fix: use newtype Name(String) with smart constructor validating non-empty; parse value at boundary or use bounded newtype; add domain validation

findings.problem: No max_items cap or try_reserve on Vec; unbounded collection from file input
findings.failure_mode: arbitrarily large file causes unbounded heap allocation, potential OOM DoS
findings.fix: accept max_items: usize parameter, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after validation, enforce cap before pushing

findings.problem: stdout println inside data-loading function — hidden I/O surface
findings.failure_mode: side effects in domain-adjacent code break pure-function guarantees, complicate testing, and produce observable behavior changes across environments
findings.fix: remove stdout I/O; pass a logging abstraction or return metadata separately from the shell layer

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for the load_frames path
findings.failure_mode: performance claims (if any) are unsupported; allocation pattern (Vec<String> per field + collect) may be suboptimal
findings.fix: add criterion or similar benchmark measuring file I/O + parse throughput and peak allocation for representative inputs

findings.problem: No tests exist; no cargo check, clippy, or test evidence available
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify correctness, lint compliance, or that fixes actually resolve the findings
findings.fix: add at minimum: compile check, clippy with strict gates, and behavior tests for empty file, malformed lines, overflow values, and valid input
